# Flow 3: the shell finds git in two places, and the Captain chooses which one the vessel uses.
#
# Two different git executables are on the PATH. Orbiter does not guess: it asks the Captain to
# choose, records that path, and from then on gives the integration exactly that binary.

step set up: the vessel, a project that uses git, and a second git on the PATH
exec orbiter --output json vessel init -y
exec orbiter --output json galaxy add acme
exec orbiter --output json planet add api --galaxy acme
exec orbiter --output json resource add git --role tool --brand git
exec orbiter --output json attach git api
env PATH=$PATH:$WORK/bin2

step calibrate: the run needs git found
client -- calibrate api
stdout '"status":"needs_discovery"'
capture SESSION '"session":"([0-9a-z]+)"'
capture TXN '"txn":"([0-9a-z]+)","op":"FIND_BINARY"'

step the shell answers with every git it finds, in PATH order
exec $FLOW_SHELL -c 'eval "$(orbiter shell init)"; FIND_BINARY "$TXN" git'

step uplink asks the Captain to choose between them; the client picks the second
client -select=2 -- uplink --session=$SESSION
stdout '"op":"SELECT"'
stdout 'Multiple locations found for git'
stdout '/bin/git'
stdout '/bin2/git'

step the second git is the one on record
exec orbiter --output json survey api -v
stdout '"binaries":\{"git":"[^"]*/bin2/git"\}'

step a later scan uses exactly that binary and finds it healthy
client -- scan api
stdout '"status":"healthy"'
stdout '"binary_path":"[^"]*/bin2/git"'
